title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 94-98). Grothendieck is studying what he calls 'disjoncteurs'. The transcription renders this word as 'disposant', but the hand reads 'disj..teur', and the next page writes 'disjoncteur'. A disjoncteur is a set E with a symmetric disjointness (orthogonality) relation x|∘|y. To it he attaches 'spatios' Σ_E: the subsets closed under the biorthogonal (polarity) closure A ↦ A^⊥⊥. These form a complete lattice with a complementation C. Morphisms ('correspondances') E → E' are relations R ⊂ E×E' with R(x) ∈ Σ_{E'} for all x and ᵗR(x') ∈ Σ_E for all x'. Equivalently, they are maps Σ_E → Σ_{E'} commuting with arbitrary Sup, whose transpose gives the self-duality noted on p. 96.

This page tests the guiding 'trivial' case. When x|∘|y ⟺ x≠y, we get Σ_E = P(E), and correspondences are arbitrary relations, i.e. elements of P(E×E'). P(E×E') is itself the spatio of the trivial disjoncteur E×E'.

He proposes to generalise via a product disjoncteur on E×E': (x,x')|∘|(y,y') ⟺ x|∘|y or x'|∘|y'. For trivial factors this gives exactly (x,x')≠(y,y'), so it recovers the motivating case.

He then checks that every closed set R ∈ Σ_{E×E'} is a correspondence. This is correct. If R = S^⊥, then R(x) = {x' : x'⊥y' for all (y,y') ∈ S with ¬(x⊥y)}, which is an orthogonal, hence closed. The same argument works for ᵗR(x').

He doubts the converse, i.e. that every bi-closed relation is closed in the product, except in the trivial case. He then retreats to a weaker question: does Corr(E,E') = Corr(Σ,Σ') carry its own structure of 'spatio'?

The next page answers part of this. With the pointwise order, Corr(Σ,Σ') is a complete lattice with pointwise Sup; this is the internal hom of sup-lattices. The complementation and disjunction structure is unclear except when E is trivial, where Corr ≅ Σ'^E with termwise C.

In modern terms: orthogonality spaces (Dacey / Foulis–Randall), equivalently formal contexts and their concept lattices. The product is exactly Wille's 'direct product of contexts' (g1,g2) I (m1,m2) ⟺ g1 I1 m1 or g2 I2 m2. Bi-closed relations are 'bonds' (Galois connections), and the question is whether the extents of the direct product exhaust the bonds. This is the classical comparison between the tensor product of complete lattices and the lattice of Galois connections.
errors: The defining formula as written, '(x,x')|∘|(y,y') ⟺ x|∘|x' ou y|∘|y'', mixes components of E and E'. The intended (and only type-correct) definition is x|∘|y or x'|∘|y'.

The suggestion that the converse (bi-closed relations are closed in the product) holds only when E ≃ E' is trivial is too restrictive. If just one factor, say E, is trivial, then the closed sets of E×E' are exactly the relations with every fibre R(x) closed, so the converse holds. The next page implicitly uses this (Corr(Σ_E,Σ') ≅ Σ'^E). The converse is also known to hold under finiteness / double-foundedness hypotheses in formal concept analysis.

ideas.what: Disjoncteur = set with symmetric disjointness relation; spatio = lattice of biorthogonally closed subsets with complementation
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space and its ortholattice of closed subsets; formal context / concept lattice via polarity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Dacey (1968); Foulis–Randall (1970s); Wille / Ganter (formal concept analysis, 1982 ff.)

ideas.what: Correspondences between disjoncteurs as relations with closed fibres in both directions, equivalently Sup-preserving maps between spatios
ideas.modern_name: Bonds / Galois connections between closure systems; morphisms in Sup; Chu-space-like morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ore (1944), Shmuely (1974), Wille / Ganter (bonds), Joyal–Tierney (1984) for Sup

ideas.what: Product disjoncteur (x,x')⊥(y,y') iff x⊥y or x'⊥y', whose closed sets are correspondences
ideas.modern_name: Direct product of formal contexts; tensor product of orthogonality spaces / complete lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wille (tensor product of concept lattices, 1985); Shmuely (1974); Foulis–Randall / Golfin (tensor products of orthoalgebras)

ideas.what: Question whether bonds coincide with closed sets of the product, and whether Corr(Σ,Σ') carries its own spatio structure (internal hom)
ideas.modern_name: Tensor product vs Galois-connection lattice comparison; closedness of the category of sup-lattices / orthomodular tensor product problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shmuely; Wille; Ganter–Wille textbook; quantum-logic tensor-product literature (Aerts, Randall–Foulis)

missed.claim: Independently of formal concept analysis and quantum logic, Grothendieck (1986) arrives at the direct product of contexts and the 'extents of the product vs bonds' problem. He motivates it via a self-dual category of 'topos-like' lattices (p. 96) with an explicit Hilbert-space adjoint analogy. The mathematics is known, but the link of his 'disjoncteur / spatio' programme to FCA and quantum-logic tensor products is not recorded anywhere.
missed.quote: Il serait tentant donc, dans le cas général, de considérer de E à E' les correspondances de disjoncteurs comme les éléments des spatios associé au "disjoncteur produit" E×E'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck rediscovering the orthogonality-space tensor-product problem. The underlying results are already in Shmuely, Wille, and Ganter–Wille.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, elementary rediscovery of known structures (orthogonality spaces, bonds, direct product of contexts, tensor product of complete lattices). The open question he poses has a known answer in the FCA literature. It is of interest only as a historical curiosity within the 'Ateliers' notes.
transcription_corrections: 'disposant' throughout should read 'disjoncteur' (e.g. 'correspondances de disjoncteurs', 'disjoncteur trivial', 'disjoncteur produit'), consistent with the next page.
'espaces[?]' should read 'spatios' (e.g. 'qui est lui-même un spatio', 'éléments des spatios associés', 'corr. de spatios Σ→Σ'').
The formula should be rendered as written, '(x,x')|∘|(y,y') ⟺ x|∘|x' ou y|∘|y'', with a note that x|∘|y ou x'|∘|y' is intended.

'On vérifie en effet que les [barré] sont dans l'ens. noté R ∈ Σ_{E×E'}' reads better as 'On vérifie en effet que les R ∈ Σ_{E×E'} sont dans l'ens. noté Corr(E,E') (p. 94) i.e. ∀x∈E, R(x)∈Σ_{E'}, et ∀x'∈E', ᵗR(x')∈Σ_E'.
'Mais il me semble pas' should read 'Mais il ne semble pas'; 'sauf dans le cas où E ≃ E' est un disjoncteur trivial'.
'Mais si ce n'était pas vrai en général' is better read as 'Mais si cela n'était pas vrai en général'.
'l'ens. des disj. corr. de E à E', ou des ensembles corr. des spatios Σ→Σ'': the crossed-out word is 'applications', replaced by 'corr.'.
The last lines read roughly 'La relation d'ordre sous-jacente au cas ensembliste (disj. triviaux) [est] l'inclusion', continued on p. 98.
